mannar-thambapavani-wind-adb.conditions_add: ADB's own loan paper for the Mannar wind farm set terms for the Ceylon Electricity Board. The resettlement plan had to be updated once the final turbine designs were ready, and CEB had to send ADB resettlement monitoring reports twice a year. The environmental management plan had to be written into the civil works contracts, and a biodiversity management plan was required to "ensure no net loss of biodiversity at the wind power generation site", with turbines switched off during the bird migration period. CEB also had to set up a project management unit and send ADB environmental monitoring reports every three months during building (Asian Development Bank, Report and Recommendation of the President, 2017).

why.safeguard: a biodiversity management plan was required to "ensure no net loss of biodiversity at the wind power generation site"
why.admin: CEB also had to set up a project management unit

east-west-highway-khevi.conditions_add: For the Shorapani-Argveta section, ADB's loan paper says a land acquisition and resettlement plan was already being carried out and that a corrective action plan would cover the gaps against ADB's resettlement rules for this project. The Roads Department's supervision consultants had to "prepare semiannual safeguards monitoring reports for ADB's review and disclosure". Georgia also had to keep "adequate and separate project records and accounts", audited each year by an independent auditor, and buy all contracts under ADB's procurement policy (Asian Development Bank, Report and Recommendation of the President, 2020).

kashang-hydro-lippa-adb.conditions_add: ADB's $800 million facility paid out in tranches, and each project had to pass a list of tests before ADB would release money. Among them were "a land acquisition and resettlement plan that meets the requirements of ADB's Involuntary Resettlement Policy (2005)", an indigenous peoples development plan, and an environmental impact assessment with an environmental management and monitoring plan, all submitted to ADB for review and made public 120 days before the state asked for the next tranche. The state power company also had to keep separate accounts for each project, and the state had to on-lend the money "under arm's-length terms to ensure commercial discipline". Civil works had to be bought by international competitive bidding (Asian Development Bank, Report and Recommendation of the President, 2008).

noor-ouarzazate-pasture.conditions_add: The World Bank's 2014 loan agreements for the Noor II and Noor III plants carried covenants. Before civil works, Morocco's solar agency had to prepare land acquisition plans and finish the measures in them, including "full payment of compensation", and could not authorise building before the plant's environmental and social impact assessment was prepared and made public. It had to send the Bank an environmental and social management report "on a bi-annual basis" during building. Money could not be drawn for a plant until the power purchase agreement and the power sale agreement for it were signed, and the agency's "Equity shall remain positive on a yearly basis" (World Bank, Project Appraisal Document, 2014).

mahenge-graphite-ulanga-faru.conditions_add: Black Rock's filing on the US$179 million facilities signed in September 2024 lists the conditions the lenders set. Before the first drawdown the company must put in the required project equity and carry out "implementation of technical, environmental and social actions", and the Bank of Tanzania must approve the agreement. From first production the borrower must hold equity support, by letter of credit or cash reserve, covering the next 12 months of debt service, rising to 24 months if sales cover is short, and must have "sufficient offtake agreements in place to provide 1x debt service cover". Each facility is limited to set uses: the term loan to "Mahenge construction costs and other eligible costs", the bank guarantee facility to "Mine closure and rehabilitation obligations" (Black Rock Mining, ASX announcement, 2024).

haiti-creole-pig-eradication.conditions_add: The eradication agreement signed by Haiti's government and the Interamerican Institute for Cooperation in Agriculture said owners of slaughtered hogs were to be compensated "prior to the depopulation stage of the Project", which Multinational Monitor says did not happen. To get a replacement pig a farmer had to be unable to buy one, agree to learn how to care for it, build a pen of suitable materials, guarantee that pigs could not reach human waste, and return one pig from the second-generation litter to the distribution centre. The contract forbade feeding animals "wastes or other ingredients which are not part of the formula" (Multinational Monitor).
